summary: Pointe Duthie Light, New Richmond on the Baie des Chaleurs: built 1903, lit 1904, dark from 1914. The tower on the point is a 1989 replica on a town heritage site.

structures.type: enclosed wooden tower, square in plan, sloping sides, square wooden lantern
structures.note: Painted white. Taken down in sections (1914 per the Quebec register; 1918 per Lighthouse Friends).
Built near the original site, incorporating surviving sections.

access.note: Town site open to visitors; Lighthouse Friends (older) says grounds open and tower closed.

stay.note: The town's site invites visitors to spend a night in the lighthouse; other buildings on the site rent by the day or week in summer. Not verified for the current season.

events.note: Tower erected by day labour under P. A. Perron, Department of Public Works engineer, at a cost of $1,798.65.
B. V. Willett, first keeper per Lighthouse Friends. Marine list gives the date as '16, 1903' with a ditto month carried from the line above (October); checked on the page image.
Put in operation on the opening of navigation in 1904.
James R. Doddridge replaced Willett; Lighthouse Friends says the change followed a change of government majority.
Light discontinued after the bay silted up following timber cutting on the Grand Cascapedia River.
Light moved to Maria, another harbour on the bay (Quebec register).

Tower taken down in sections (Quebec register gives 1914; Lighthouse Friends gives 1918). Upper and middle sections to the Carswell farm; the upper section later burned; the lower section to a property at Dimock Creek.
Replica built by the Gaspesian British Heritage Centre using surviving sections, near the original site.
Quebec register: the lighthouse is located within a heritage site, status dated 8 April 2002.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Quebec register and Lighthouse Friends give 1903 for the tower's construction. The Marine report of 1904 says the light was put in operation at the opening of navigation in 1904. Both fit: built 1903, first lit 1904.
The Quebec register gives 1914 for the tower's dismantling (the light moved to Maria that year). Lighthouse Friends gives 1918. Not resolved; the story gives both.
The register calls the 1989 replica a rebuilding of 'the 1911 lighthouse'. No other source here gives a tower of 1911; the register's own tower date is 1903. Flagged, not resolved.
The Marine report (1904) says the whole tower was painted white. Lighthouse Friends describes a lantern 'trimmed in red'. Could be a later repainting; not resolved.

Lighthouse Friends says the lighthouse is owned by the Gaspesian British Heritage Village. The town's listing presents the site as Ville de New Richmond, and the station record names the town as agency. Lighthouse Friends is older, so the town's listing is taken as current.
Lighthouse Friends (older) says the tower is closed. The town's listing invites visitors to spend a night in the lighthouse. Current status not verified by a dated source.

notes_for_editor: Sources: Lighthouse Friends is a community site (facts only). The Quebec register records are the most official sources here: the secteur record (no. 167321) gives the history and the 1989 date; the lighthouse record (no. 166504) gives the 1989 construction date and the 2002 status. The Marine report (Thirty-Seventh Annual Report, 1904, p. 38) is the only primary source on the tower's build and first light, and it is clean OCR for the description and cost. Keeper matching is by column position in the Marine list (p. 158, scan 171): checked on the page image on 2026-10-27, the Willett row reads 'Willett, B. V' against 'New Richmond, Duthie Point', with the appointment '16, 1903' under a ditto mark for the month carried from the line above (Oct. 18, 1889), so October 16, 1903. The report is for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1904 (printed 1905, Sessional Paper A. 1905). James R. Doddridge (1911) was not found in the corpus text I searched, so his entry rests on Lighthouse Friends alone. The Marine report's 12-mile visibility does not state statute or nautical miles, so no range_nm is given. Lighthouse Friends gives the focal height as 50 feet; 15.2 m in the record is the conversion. The French Wikipedia article is used for leads only, and it says the light was to be moved in 2015 because of erosion (citing L'Écho de la Baie, 2015); that article was not read and needs checking before any mention. The register's inventory of Quebec lighthouses (2009-2010) is listed but not read. The town's note that a night in the lighthouse is possible is undated and was not verified; check the season and booking with the town before publishing as current. Jim Dimock (land at Dimock Creek) is a private landowner and is not named in the story. The routedesphares listing 'Autres noms: Phare de Pointe Taylor' is not used. Corpus search for Doddridge in 1911-1915 volumes found nothing; the Marine lists for those years were not checked by position. No photos added.
